feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: clear positioning, solid career progression, and relevant technical breadth. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive and could be sharper on measurable impact, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level brand: the header summary aligns well with the experience and presents a focused Digital Communications & Strategy Lead profile.  
- Strong credibility and progression: multiple promotions within NACo show trust, growth, and increasing leadership scope.  
- Good substance and specificity: Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, Clarity, Power BI, studio buildout, and website scale metrics add technical and operational weight.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcomes, not just responsibilities: several bullets describe what you led or built, but fewer show results such as engagement growth, efficiency gains, campaign performance, or stakeholder impact.  
- Reduce duplication and tighten structure: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidating these would improve scannability.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “more than 12 years experience” should be “more than 12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; punctuation in lists is inconsistent (e.g., “web, email, social, and multimedia” vs. no Oxford comma elsewhere); “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—use “A2 (learning)” or “Elementary (A2).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning, but it’s slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and adding a more distinctive leadership/value angle would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Revise to: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Specializes in cross-channel communications, platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and systems that enable complex teams to operate effectively. Brings deep experience in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical and policy issues into clear, accessible content.”
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Use “leader” instead of “professional” to better match senior roles like Director and Consultant.
- Add “governance” because it is a recurring strength in recent roles and sharpens your positioning.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “stakeholder coordination” are repeated in Core Competencies/Topline Skills.
- Avoid adding tools or channel lists beyond this; those are already well covered elsewhere.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening wording and emphasizing higher-value leadership/modernization strengths will make it sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic phrases with more senior, specific language: “Multi-channel communication” → “Cross-channel communications leadership”; “Web & CMS administration” → “Web platform modernization & CMS management.”
- Reduce overlap and group related items: combine “Editorial workflow design” and “Workflow & systems architecture” into one stronger competency.
- Align style/pluralization for consistency: use parallel noun phrases throughout.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform modernization & CMS management • Editorial operations, workflow & governance • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia, video & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the header.
- “Digital strategy & transformation” and analytics/workflow themes are already covered in Topline Skills; keep this version concise, not exhaustive.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good strategic/technical breadth, but it reads too much like a responsibility list and overlaps heavily with earlier NACo roles and the Recent Projects section. Tighten it around consultant-level outcomes, scope, and what is new since returning in 2024.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper positioning line: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, and cross-channel content operations as an external consultant.”
- Replace generic verbs (“consult,” “advise,” “deliver”) with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Streamlined,” “launched,” “designed,” “implemented,” “led.”
- Consolidate into 3–4 bullets focused on distinct contributions: digital systems/workflows, Drupal campaign builds, AI-enabled search, and governance/usability improvements.
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/microsites launched, workflow time reduced, toolkit downloads, search accuracy/engagement gains, stakeholder teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, and enterprise web improvement” repeats the Director of Digital Media entry; emphasize external advisory scope and new initiatives instead.
- Microsites and AI search already appear in Recent Projects, so keep this item higher-level and outcome-focused rather than project-detail heavy.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize enterprise ownership and outcomes while avoiding overlap with the adjacent NACo roles on newsletters, video, and general digital operations.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget across enterprise platforms.”
- Prioritize the biggest wins first and make them outcome-led: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Strengthen impact language on analytics/governance: “Built a cross-platform analytics stack (GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, BigQuery) to improve executive reporting, content decisions, and performance visibility.”
- Make the studio bullet more results-oriented if possible: add output or cost/time savings (e.g., increased production volume, reduced vendor reliance, expanded event coverage).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry at the enterprise/leadership level.
- Video-programming language may duplicate older NACo entries; focus here on building institutional capacity, not recurring production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story and good channel breadth, but this entry reads generic and overlaps heavily with the more senior NACo roles. Tighten it around what was distinctly built or expanded at this level.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and cross-team editorial execution.”
- Combine and sharpen bullets around owned outputs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and outcome-focused: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “helped improve” with direct contribution: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Led digital communications across web, email, social media and video” is too close to the Director of Digital Media entry.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it largely repeats the header and Core Competencies. Make it sharper, more distinctive, and aligned to recent leadership scope rather than broad communications phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Replace with more specific, higher-signal bullets:
- Enterprise digital strategy and web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social and video
- Public-sector digital communications and advocacy campaigns
- Consider dropping “Audience-focused content planning”; it reads junior compared with director/consultant-level experience.
- Use parallel noun phrases and avoid generic terms like “messaging” unless tied to campaigns, advocacy, or stakeholder audiences.
- If space allows, add scale in adjacent experience bullets instead of here; skills sections should stay crisp, not descriptive.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps heavily with multiple NACo roles; keep this item focused on strategic leadership, not channel execution.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill set, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes rather than listing every technology.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • Website modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Remove lower-priority or older-signal items like jQuery unless it is still central to current work.
- Put the strongest, most recent differentiators first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/automation.
- If space allows, sharpen with scope language tied to recent work: “Enterprise Drupal platforms,” “large-scale CMS modernization,” or “cross-system workflow automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, HTML/CSS/JavaScript, API integrations, and Airtable already appear in Technical + IT.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also overlaps with Core Competencies and recent project content.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize strategic analytics capability, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to a capability-led line, e.g.: “Analytics strategy, dashboarding and performance optimization: GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO analysis.”
- Put the highest-value/most strategic terms first: “Analytics strategy,” “KPI design,” and “executive reporting” before individual tools.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” for clearer, more standard phrasing.
- Consider “SEO and performance analysis” → “SEO and digital performance analysis” for precision.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills more strategic and leave the full tool stack there.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact framing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and the in-house studio/event leadership angle.

Suggested edit
- Replace task-style terms with capability/outcome phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production,” “Livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “Studio build-out and operations,” “PTZ/multi-camera production.”
- Reorder by strategic value and recency: lead with studio/event production and livestreaming, then video/editing, then technical systems.
- Consider a tighter version: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • Studio operations and build-out • PTZ and multi-camera systems”
- If space allows, add scale/context elsewhere rather than here (e.g., in experience bullets): in-house studio creation, recurring advocacy programming, event support.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Livestreaming” overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Multimedia production and livestream operations”; vary wording or keep detail in only one place.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” is close to “event production” already demonstrated in recent NACo roles and projects.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. Since Drupal is clearly the strongest and most recent platform in the CV, that emphasis should come through here.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider signaling depth: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of just names: **Drupal site architecture, microsites, migrations • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Keep this item platform-focused; avoid mixing in broader capabilities already covered elsewhere.
- If you want more impact, tie Drupal to scale in experience bullets rather than here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially overlaps with **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider trimming one or making this version more platform-only.
- “CMS modernization” is already listed elsewhere, so don’t add it here unless removing it from Topline Skills.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior, recent-profile CV, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from raw coding languages to applied implementation: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless used elsewhere consistently; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner.
- If accurate, add scope or outcomes in adjacent experience bullets instead of here, e.g., integrations deployed, workflows automated, or performance/reliability gains enabled by Workers/GitHub Actions.
- Put the strongest, more current tools first: Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • HTML/CSS/JavaScript • jQuery

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Google Tag Manager” may also overlap conceptually with analytics infrastructure elsewhere; keep only if actively used hands-on.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function and keep only strongest, most relevant platforms: “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier • Project/issue management: Jira, Asana • Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- Cut lower-value or older/generic tools unless used heavily in recent roles: Basecamp, Trello
- If space allows, add a light qualifier tied to impact: “used to support cross-team publishing, approvals, and communications operations”
- Consider renaming the heading to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” for clearer alignment with your recent work

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same language verbatim
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; keep them only if they materially support your systems/operations positioning

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. It should signal level of use and enterprise relevance, especially since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to group by function and sharpen platform credibility: “Email marketing automation & member engagement: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys, Higher Logic, Mailchimp”
- If accurate, add scope/level in brief parentheticals: “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (enterprise campaign automation), Higher Logic (member communications), Mailchimp (newsletter operations)”
- Put the strongest/most enterprise platform first; keep Dynamics 365 first unless Higher Logic was more central in recent roles.
- Consider aligning naming with current product branding exactly and keep separators consistent across Technical + IT items.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters and multi-channel communications; avoid adding outcome claims here unless they are not already stated elsewhere.
- “Engagement” may feel vague given Higher Logic already implies member engagement; “Email marketing automation & member engagement” is tighter.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too broad and repeats themes already covered in later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to what was first built or launched during this earlier period.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize foundational contributions: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media function, improving coordination across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add 1–2 concrete outputs: website refresh support, livestream production, weekly video series, team/process improvements.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce soft language like “high-impact” and “strengthening”; replace with actions and scope.
- If possible, add metrics: number of livestreams/events produced, frequency of video updates, audience growth, or workflow/time savings.

Possible rewrite:
- Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital media team and support a major website refresh.
- Produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, expanding the organization’s multimedia and advocacy communications capacity.
- Improved day-to-day workflows across web, email, social and video, and provided direct guidance to a digital media associate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating newsletter/editorial coordination language from the 2018–2022 role.
- Avoid overclaiming team leadership, which is better reserved for the later director role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize coordination scope and the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout result: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Tighten the second sentence and make the podcast launch the capstone: “Supported digital and multimedia content production, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add scale or output: number of projects supported, episodes produced, stakeholders served, or audience/download growth.
- Consider a more active, concise version: “Managed innovation/research projects and produced digital content; launched NACo’s first podcast from concept through production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item lighter and more foundational.
- Avoid overemphasizing video/multimedia here since those strengths are better demonstrated in 2015–2024 roles.
